gap: No result ChatGPT got states any named reviewer's measured capacity, range or voltage sag for a budget 48V pack. I couldn't source one either, so the best I can add is that two named YouTube bench tests exist (Gavin Stone DIY Homestead on the LiTime 48V 100Ah, Mike Builds on the WEIZE 48V 105Ah) and that GolferHive ran a 4-week LiTime test without publishing any figures.
standout_why: Compared against our own page (dealectric.com/best-golf-cart-lithium-battery), golfcartgearlab.com, golfcartshowdown.com and the cited LiTime product page. golfcartgearlab says its editors tested nothing, and every figure on it is a brand spec. golfcartshowdown reports only maker amp ratings; it lists a Will Prowse video on a RoyPow pack in its sources but quotes no figure from it. Our page already says it has no independent capacity or sag data, and its only 'measured' figure is LiTime's own range test (109.73 Wh/mile). gearranking.com would not load (certificate error), so it was not checked. No rival has a named third-party measurement. Mine has names and test lengths but no figures, so it adds very little.
decides: Nothing here changes the pick. No named reviewer has published a capacity, range or sag figure in text for NewtiPower, Redodo, LiTime, ECO-WORTHY, WEIZE, CHINS or Vatrer, so measurements can't separate the budget packs. The pick has to rest on maker BMS ratings (LiTime 100 A continuous vs 200 A BMS on NewtiPower, Redodo, WEIZE and Vatrer), price and warranty. The page can honestly say that no independent capacity test of these budget packs is published in text.
